$comment: Free starter prompts bundled with FlowCompanion and written for it. They are labelled as bundled in the app; there are no ratings, reviews or download counts for them.

creator.bio: Free prompts written for and bundled with FlowCompanion. Use, change and share them freely.

listings.title: Explain a topic from scratch
listings.summary: A clear explanation pitched at your level, with an example and a quick self-check.
listings.body:
Explain {{topic}} to someone at a {{level:beginner}} level.

1. Start with a one-sentence plain-language summary.
2. Explain the key ideas step by step, defining any jargon the first time you use it.
3. Give one concrete, everyday example.
4. List two common misconceptions and why they are wrong.
5. End with three short questions I can use to check my understanding (answers at the very end).

If you are unsure about a fact, say so instead of guessing.

listings.title: Build a study plan
listings.summary: Turns a goal and the time you have into a realistic, week-by-week plan.

listings.title: Quiz me
listings.summary: An interactive quiz that asks one question at a time and explains mistakes.
listings.body:
Quiz me on {{topic}}.

- Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer.
- Mix recall, understanding and application questions, starting easy.
- After each answer, tell me if I was right, explain briefly, and adjust the difficulty.
- After {{number of questions:8}} questions, summarise what I know well and what to review.

listings.title: Summarise a text
listings.summary: A faithful summary with key points, open questions and nothing invented.
listings.body:
Summarise the text below for {{audience:a busy reader}}.

Give:
1. A two-sentence overview.
2. The key points as bullets, in the order the text makes them.
3. Any claims that would need checking, and why.

Only use what is in the text. If something is unclear, say so rather than filling the gap.

Text:
"""
{{text}}
"""

listings.title: Check claims against sources
listings.summary: Separates claims into supported, unsupported and needs-checking, with search suggestions.
listings.body:
Here is a paragraph I want to use:

"""
{{paragraph}}
"""

List each factual claim it makes. For each one say whether it is common knowledge, needs a source, or looks doubtful, and suggest what I could search for to verify it. Do not invent sources or citations.

listings.title: Feedback on my writing
listings.summary: Specific, prioritised feedback that keeps your voice — without rewriting it for you.
listings.body:
Give me feedback on the {{kind of writing:essay draft}} below. My goal for it: {{goal:make the argument clearer}}.

- Start with what works well.
- Then give the three most important improvements, each with an example from my text.
- Point out any unclear sentences.

Do not rewrite the whole piece; I want to keep my own voice.

"""
{{text}}
"""

listings.title: Draft a clear email
listings.summary: A short, polite email with a clear request and subject line.

listings.title: Rewrite in plain language
listings.summary: Makes dense text easier to read while keeping the meaning.
listings.body:
Rewrite the text below in plain language for {{audience:a general reader}}.

- Use short sentences and common words.
- Keep every fact and instruction; do not add new information.
- Explain any technical term that must stay.

Afterwards, list anything you were unsure how to simplify without changing the meaning.

"""
{{text}}
"""

listings.title: Turn notes into actions
listings.summary: Extracts decisions, action items with owners, and open questions from rough notes.
listings.body:
From the meeting notes below, extract:

1. Decisions made
2. Action items as a checklist: what, who, and by when (write "not stated" if missing — do not guess)
3. Open questions
4. A three-sentence summary I can send to people who missed it

Notes:
"""
{{notes}}
"""

listings.title: Plan my day
listings.summary: Orders your tasks into a realistic schedule with focus blocks and breaks.
listings.body:
Here are my tasks for today:
{{tasks}}

I have from {{start time:9:00}} to {{end time:17:00}}, with these fixed commitments: {{commitments:none}}.

Suggest a realistic schedule: put the hardest work in my best focus time ({{best focus time:the morning}}), group small tasks together, add short breaks, and leave some slack. Tell me which tasks to drop or move if it does not all fit.

listings.title: Think through a decision
listings.summary: Structured pros, cons, risks and questions — the decision stays yours.

listings.title: Explain this code
listings.summary: A walkthrough of what code does, its edge cases and possible bugs.
listings.body:
Explain what this {{language}} code does, for someone with {{experience:some programming experience}}.

1. A one-paragraph overview.
2. A walkthrough of the important parts.
3. Edge cases or inputs that could break it.
4. Any bugs or risky patterns you notice, marked as "likely" or "possible".

```
{{code}}
```

listings.title: Help me debug
listings.summary: Systematic hypotheses and checks instead of guesswork.

listings.title: Write test cases
listings.summary: Test ideas covering normal cases, edge cases and failures.
listings.body:
Suggest test cases for this {{language}} function, using {{test framework:the usual test framework for this language}}.

Cover typical inputs, edge cases (empty, very large, invalid) and expected failures. For each test, say what it checks and why it matters. Then write the tests.

```
{{code}}
```

listings.title: Reply to a customer
listings.summary: An empathetic, accurate reply that does not over-promise.

listings.title: Write a product description
listings.summary: Honest, benefit-focused copy based only on the facts you provide.
listings.body:
Write a product description for {{product}}, aimed at {{audience}}.

Facts about the product (use only these, do not invent features or claims):
{{facts}}

Give a headline, a 60–90 word description and three bullet points of benefits. Avoid exaggerated claims; note any claim that would need evidence before publishing.
